_comment: The suite the team already had, checked in and running long before anybody
pointed an agent at this API. It is here because an agent that writes tests
does not replace the tests you have - it adds to them.
Two things worth knowing about a file like this. It is where a team's
hard-won cases live: the load-shaped one nobody wants to write twice, the
one added the morning after an incident. And it is where stale cases hide -
written against a contract that has since moved on, still green because
nothing has forced them to be re-read.

cases.name: orders: 101 calls in a minute is rate limited, with Retry-After
cases.traces_to: STORY-4501: more than 100 requests per minute from one client receives 429, and the 429 must carry Retry-After
cases._why_here: Load-shaped, slow to write, and nobody wants to write it twice. Exactly the kind of case that lives in a regression file rather than being regenerated.

cases.name: orders: a second customer's orders are readable
cases.traces_to: STORY-4471: the case screen shows recent orders
cases._why_here: Added after an incident where one customer's orders were readable and another's were not.

cases.name: notes: adding a note to a closed case returns 400

body.text: Customer called back about the refund.

cases.traces_to: STORY-4520: a closed case is read-only
cases._why_here: STALE. Written when the API returned 400 for this. The contract was later corrected to 409, because the request is well-formed and it is the case's state that refuses it - and nobody came back to update this case. The test is wrong; the API is right.

cases.name: case: an unknown case id is not found
cases.traces_to: GET /cases/{case_id}: 404 when no case has that identifier

cases.name: case: a fresh case reports note_count 0
cases.traces_to: R-COUNT: a case reports note_count, the number of notes currently on it
cases._why_here: Passes on its own. Fails after any case that adds a note to CASE-1001, because the two share state. Written by somebody who ran it alone.
